title: Schizophrenia, schizoaffective and bipolar disorder
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM code for the patient's psychiatric condition.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for mood stability.

HPI
The patient is an 86-year-old male who presents today for a follow-up evaluation of his bipolar disorder. He reports that his mood has been consistently low over the past several weeks. He describes feeling persistently depressed and mentions a significant lack of interest in his usual hobbies and social activities. He notes that his energy levels are low and he finds it difficult to initiate daily tasks. He denies any thoughts of self-harm or harm to others. He reports that while his mood is low, he remains oriented and has not experienced any significant changes in his perception of reality. He reports that his current symptoms are moderate in intensity and have persisted despite his current regimen. He is seeking an adjustment to his medication to help stabilize his mood.

Medication List
- Lamotrigine 200 mg daily
- Quetiapine 50 mg at bedtime

Review of Systems
The patient reports a positive history for low mood and fatigue. He denies any chest pain, shortness of breath, or recent weight changes. He denies any tremors, insomnia, or changes in appetite. He denies any significant neurological complaints.

Social History
The patient lives at home with his wife. He is retired and spends most of his time gardening and reading. He does not smoke and does not drink alcohol.

Family History
His father had a history of hypertension and his mother had a history of heart disease. There is no known family history of psychiatric conditions.

Vitals
Blood Pressure: 132/82 mmHg
Heart Rate: 74 bpm
Temperature: 98.6 F
SpO2: 97% on room air
Weight: 175 lbs

Recent Labs
HbA1c: 6.2%
TSH: 2.1 mIU/L
eGFR: 65 mL/min/1.73m2

Exam
The patient appears well-groomed and is dressed appropriately for the weather. He is cooperative and maintains good eye contact. His speech is normal in rate, volume, and tone. His affect is congruent with his reported mood. He demonstrates a moderate level of psychomotor slowing. He is alert and oriented to person, place, and time.

Assessment
The patient is an 86-year-old male with bipolar disorder who is currently experiencing a depressed mood. His symptoms are moderate in severity. He has shown limited response to his current dose of lamotrigine.

Plan
1. Increase lamotrigine dosage to 300 mg daily to address current symptoms.
2. Continue current dose of quetiapine.
3. Follow up in four weeks to monitor response to the medication increase and assess for any side effects.

Electronically signed,
P. O'Brien, PA-C
May 14, 2026
explanations: Bipolar disorder, current episode depressed, moderate: F31.32 (HCC 154).

distractors.why: A depressed episode of bipolar disorder is coded in F31, not as major depression.
The episode and severity are documented.
